title: Spin lettuce dry in a hand-crank salad spinner: hold the bowl, keep the loose lid on, spin out two-thirds of its water
instruction: Spin the washed lettuce dry in the salad spinner: crank it clockwise fast enough and long enough to spin out at least two-thirds of the water the lettuce carries (the basket well over 5 turns a second for about 6 seconds), keep the lid on, then let go of the crank.
context: Spinning washed greens dry is routine in home cooking and a core prep step for food preparation workers (O*NET 35-2021.00) and cooks. A crank on the lid drives the basket through 1:5 gears and a one-way clutch. What dries the leaves is the outward push at the basket's wall, which goes with the square of its speed, so the score is by water: the share of what the lettuce carried in that has been spun out, weighed on a kitchen scale in a real trial. Slow cranking leaves it wet. So the hand must take a small knob round a 5.5 cm circle more than once a second, a dozen times, going where the crank goes. The lid only lies on the bowl: pulling up or sideways on the knob lifts it off and the crank then drives nothing. The gears push back, so the light bowl turns with the crank unless the other hand holds its handle, a precondition the instruction leaves unsaid.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). A 2-quart hand-crank salad spinner, base centred at x 32, y -7. Bowl: clear plastic, 20 cm across, 11 cm tall, 0.13 kg, plain plastic base on the worktop (friction about 0.25); a green rubber-faced side handle 6 cm out from the bowl on its +y side, 5 mm thick, 2.5 cm tall, middle 5 cm above the table; two green lugs (4 mm out, 8 mm wide, 12 mm tall) under the rim at front and back. Lid: clear, 21 cm across, 1 cm thick, 0.20 kg with its gears, lying loose on the bowl's rim; its own rim reaches 1.5 cm down round the bowl's (0.8 mm clearance) with a notch at each lug, so it cannot turn on the bowl but lifts straight off; a green gear housing (4 cm across) in its middle and a red mark near its edge. Crank: grey arm 6.6 cm long on the housing, top 13.5 cm above the table, turning about the spinner's axis; at 5.5 cm from the axis a green knob 2.2 cm across and 3.4 cm tall that turns freely; it starts pointing +x; crank and knob 0.03 kg. Basket: white, 17.6 cm across, with 150 g of washed lettuce (0.27 kg in all) and a red stripe on its rim, visible through the bowl. Gearing: with the lid on, one clockwise crank turn turns the basket 5 times through a one-way clutch; backward cranking, or cranking with the lid off the bowl, does not drive it. Both arms start in the raised ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Tools: a kitchen scale reading 1 g or better; the trial video; a ruler; a tape mark round the bowl's base. Before the trial weigh the lettuce dry (D), dunk it 10 s, let it drip 10 s in the basket and weigh it wet (W); after the trial weigh it again (E). Share of its water spun out = (W - E) / (W - D). (In simulation, which has no water, the share is worked out each step from the push at the basket's wall: see fidelity.) 0 for the whole trial if at any time the spinner's base moves 8 cm or more from its place, the spinner tilts 15 degrees or more, or the lid comes off the bowl: the lid's middle 5 mm or more above its place on the rim, or the lid tipped 8 degrees or more from the rim, or its middle 10.5 cm or more to the side of the bowl's axis (on video, the gaps between lid and rim on opposite sides of the bowl average 5 mm or more, or differ by 28 mm or more). Otherwise: 1.0 if two-thirds or more of the water has been spun out and, at the end, both grippers' tool points are 4 cm or more from the crank's knob (let go); 0.5 if half or more; 0.25 if a third or more; else 0. Turning the crank earns nothing by itself.
reset_notes: Each trial: pat about 150 g of torn lettuce dry and weigh it (D), dunk it 10 s, lift it out in the basket, let it drip 10 s and weigh it wet (W). Wipe the bowl dry, put the basket and lettuce in, lid on its lugs, crank pointing away from the robot, bowl on its tape mark. After the trial weigh the lettuce (E) and pour the bowl's water away. The same lettuce can be used again.
fidelity: Bowl (with basket) and lid (with crank and knob) are two loose rigid parts; the lid rests on the rim, held only by weight, its rim and two lugs. Gears are a rule each step: lid on, the clutch drives the basket toward 5x the crank's speed (up to 0.01 N m); else it coasts. No water is simulated. The share spun out follows a rule: at n times gravity at the wall the leaves keep n^-0.5 of it, approached over 2 s. That is a capillary argument and an estimate, not measured on a spinner.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper hovered over the lid beside the crank, the left came to the bowl's handle side; the crank was not turned); demo: 1.0 (71.5% of the water spun out, basket up to 374 rpm, lid on throughout, full score at step 465). Videos: overhead, left wrist, right wrist
